$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. RecoverySnapshot per FB-RAT-WS-001/003: the checkpoint WorkspaceJournal.checkpoint()/restore() produce/consume, existing specifically to satisfy FB-RAT-WS-003 (dirty buffers survive Activity recreation/process death/reboot until explicit save or discard). Typically carried as the `payload` of a ContractEnvelope<RecoverySnapshot>; `snapshotId` below is this object's own FB-RAT-COM-002 stable ID. `resourceUri`/`digest` sub-shapes mirror resource-uri.schema.json / schemas/common/envelope.schema.json's IntegrityRef $defs — duplicated locally rather than cross-file $ref'd, same standalone-file tradeoff COMMON_CONVENTIONS.md documents.
title: RecoverySnapshot

snapshotId.description: Globally unique stable ID for this snapshot (FB-RAT-COM-002).

takenAtUtc.description: UTC instant this snapshot was captured (FB-RAT-COM-004).

reason.description: What triggered this checkpoint. PRE_OPERATION is what a RepositoryState.operationLock's `recoverySnapshotId` points at before a history-rewriting git op begins (FB-RAT-WS-007); PROCESS_DEATH_CAPTURE is the last-resort capture a process-death/OOM-kill hook takes on the way down, best-effort by nature.

lastJournalSequence.description: The global journal watermark this snapshot represents (FB-RAT-COM-004 — monotonic sequence preferred over wall-clock). WorkspaceJournal.restore() resumes journal replay strictly after this sequence, never before, to avoid double-applying entries this snapshot already reflects.

bufferSnapshots.description: Per-buffer captured state sufficient to reconstitute every OPEN_DIRTY/SAVING/SAVE_FAILED/CONFLICTED/MERGING buffer this workspace held at capture time (FB-RAT-WS-003). A buffer that was OPEN_CLEAN/CLOSED at capture time MAY be omitted — its content is already durable at `resourceUri`, nothing to recover.

journalSequence.description: This buffer's own `journalSequence` at capture time — MUST be <= the snapshot's top-level `lastJournalSequence`.

contentDigest.description: Digest+length over the captured buffer content bytes (FB-RAT-COM-005) — the bytes themselves are persisted by whatever store WorkspaceJournal.checkpoint() writes to (implementation-specific, e.g. an app-private snapshot cache); this digest is how restore() verifies it read back exactly what was captured.

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).
